what_happened: Found that packages/sapience-flake/{modules/sapience.nix,lib/wrappers.nix} independently duplicates the memoryFiles/NO_MEMFILES option and wiring pattern that a NO_CLASSIFY toggle would need to mirror; flagged in the research report as a planning decision (update both trees or defer) rather than silently missed.

Plan-time measurement: bash .claude/scripts/verify-touched.sh on this task's own target paths fell back to the full 86-suite shell battery (suite_selection_select returns __FULL_SWEEP__ for both modules/home/services/sapience.nix and docs/sapience.md), and that battery is already red with 13 NEW failing suites under .claude/scripts/tests/ unrelated to this task, which touches no .sh file. Baseline recorded in the plan so the final full-gate phase can compare a delta rather than demanding an unobtainable all-green.

The task description says the Known gaps section of docs/sapience.md records the whole-backlog reclassify; it does not -- that text lives in ### Performance and failure modes (docs/sapience.md:511-515) and in ### Cost shape (:467-471). Both confirmed present by grep at plan time, so the plan names the real correction targets instead of sending the implementer hunting a nonexistent Known-gaps bullet.

Phase 1's new ESTIMATE comment text literally contained the substring NO_CLASSIFY=1, colliding with the plan's own grep -c 'NO_CLASSIFY=1' == 1 verification check against the sapience-bootstrap script (counted 2, not 1, since the comment line matched too). Rephrased the comment to 'NO_CLASSIFY exported' (dropping the =1 suffix) to remove the collision; rebuilt and re-verified exactly 1 per target.

Phase 2's atomic-batch edit set (lib/wrappers.nix argument + 3 export sites + ticker treatment, modules/sapience.nix option + inherit + export, flake.nix, checks/default.nix, README.md) evaluated and built cleanly on the first attempt against all 6 of the subtree's own nix flake check -L ./packages/sapience-flake checks (shellcheck, help-output, token-functions, wsl-probe, register-mcp, hm-module), with zero golden-file drift. Lesson from Phase 1 (avoid the literal NO_CLASSIFY=1 substring in prose comments) was applied up front here and confirmed by grep -c returning 0 on the vendor-default build, matching the plan's expected result exactly.

Phase 3's fresh sapience coverage run on 2026-11-18 read 'would ingest now: 136', exactly matching the figure the research report already carried from the same date -- independent confirmation that the classify-eligible backlog genuinely holds flat rather than drifting between separate inspection passes on the same day.
